title: The Longest Border of a Word

concept.title: The longest border of the whole word is the last value of the prefix function
body: A **border** of a word is a proper prefix of it that is also a suffix. The word `abcabcab` has the borders `ab` (length 2) and `abcab` (length 5); the **longest border** has length 5. The word `abcd` has no border, so the answer is 0. Checking all prefix lengths and comparing them with the suffixes costs O(n^2).

The prefix function `pi[i]` is by definition the length of the longest border of the prefix `s[0..i]`. For the whole word the answer is therefore the **last value**, `pi[n - 1]`. There is nothing else to do: the entire work is the computation of the prefix function in O(n).

The border has a useful interpretation: if the longest border has length `b`, then the word looks the same when shifted by `n - b` positions, so `n - b` is the shortest "period" of the word. This is used in the next problems on repetitions, rotations and covers.

statement: A word `s` is given. A border is a proper prefix of `s` that is also a suffix of `s` (the empty word is allowed). Print the length of the longest border.
outputFormat: Print the length of the longest border.
constraints: The word consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: A border is a proper prefix that is also a suffix; think of the prefix function.
The prefix function of the whole word holds the answer.
It is the last value pi[n - 1].

explanation: The prefix function of the whole word at its last position is the length of the longest border.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def prefix_function(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        k = pi[i - 1]
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    return pi

s = input().strip()

pi = prefix_function(s)
print(pi[-1])
